1.solutions: We use the quotient rule to compute \[f'(x) = \frac{g'(x) \cdot x - g(x) \cdot 1}{x^2}\] \[f'(2) = \frac{8 \cdot 2 - 4 \cdot 1}{2^2} = \frac{16 - 4}{4} = \boxed{3}.\]

2.solutions: We begin by applying L’Hopital’s Rule to each term in the sum \[\lim_{n \to 1} \frac{n^k - 1}{\ln(n)} = \lim_{n \to 1} \frac{k n^{k-1}}{1/n} = k.\] If we swap the limit and finite sum in our original problem, we can then compute \[\lim_{n \to 1} \sum_{k=1}^{25} \frac{n^k - 1}{\ln(n)} = \sum_{k=1}^{25} \lim_{n \to 1} \frac{n^k - 1}{\ln(n)} = \sum_{k=1}^{25} k = \frac{(25)(26)}{2} = \boxed{325}.\]

3.solutions: We first compute \[\int_0^\pi \sin^2(x) \, dx = \int_0^\pi \frac{1 - \cos(2x)}{2} \, dx = \left( \frac{x}{2} - \frac{\sin(2x)}{4} \right) \Big|_0^\pi = \frac{\pi}{2}.\] Now note that \(d(-\cos(x)) = \sin(x)\), which allows us to integrate by parts and compute \[\int_0^\pi \sin^n(x) \, dx = \int_0^\pi \sin^{n-1}(x) d(-\cos(x)) \, dx\] \[= -\sin^{n-1}(x) \cos(x) \Big|_0^\pi - \int_0^\pi (n-1) \sin^{n-2}(x)(-\cos^2(x)) \, dx\] \[= 0 + (n-1) \int_0^\pi \sin^{n-2}(x)(1 - \sin^2(x)) \, dx\] \[= (n-1) \int_0^\pi \sin^{n-2}(x) \, dx - (n-1) \int_0^\pi \sin^n(x) \, dx.\] Rearranging gives us \[\int_0^\pi \sin^n(x) \, dx = \frac{n-1}{n} \int_0^\pi \sin^{n-2}(x) \, dx.\] This gives us a recursive relation between the integrals. From above, when \(n = 2\), we have \(\int_0^\pi \sin^2(x) \, dx = \frac{\pi}{2}\). Therefore, when \(n = 10\), we have \[\frac{\pi}{2} \cdot \frac{3}{4} \cdot \frac{5}{6} \cdot \frac{7}{8} \cdot \frac{9}{10} = \boxed{\frac{63\pi}{256}}.\]
